N: Prove that a group of order 312 has a normal Sylow $p$-subgroup for some prime $p$ dividing its order.
D:
theorem exercise_4_5_14 {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]
  (hG : card G = 312) :
  ∃ (p : ℕ) (P : Sylow p G), P.Normal :=
C:
theorem exercise_4_5_14 {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G]
  (hG : card G = 312) :
  ∃ (p : ℕ) (P : Sylow p G), p.Prime ∧ (p ∣ card G) ∧ P.Normal :=
defect: Drops p prime and p | |G|; trivially true via p = 1 or p not dividing 312 (trivial Sylow subgroup is normal).; Drops p prime and p ∣ |G|; trivially satisfied by p=1 or p∤312 with P=⊥ normal.

N: Prove that a group of order 351 has a normal Sylow $p$-subgroup for some prime $p$ dividing its order.

  (hG : card G = 351) :
  ∃ (p : ℕ) (P : Sylow p G), p.Prime ∧ (p ∣ card G) ∧  P.Normal :=
defect: No requirement that p is prime dividing 351; trivial via p = 1 or a non-dividing prime.; p need not be prime or divide 351; trivially true with p = 2 (trivial Sylow 2-subgroup is normal).

N: Let $|G|=p q r$, where $p, q$ and $r$ are primes with $p<q<r$. Prove that $G$ has a normal Sylow subgroup for either $p, q$ or $r$.
D:
theorem exercise_4_5_16 {p q r : ℕ} {G : Type*} [Group G]
  [Fintype G]  (hpqr : p < q ∧ q < r)
  (hpqr1 : p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ r.Prime)(hG : card G = p*q*r) :
  Nonempty (Sylow p G) ∨ Nonempty (Sylow q G) ∨ Nonempty (Sylow r G) :=
C:
theorem exercise_4_5_16 {p q r : ℕ} {G : Type*} [Group G]
  [Fintype G]  (hpqr : p < q ∧ q < r)
  (hpqr1 : p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ r.Prime)(hG : card G = p*q*r) :
  (∃ (P : Sylow p G), P.Normal) ∨ (∃ (P : Sylow q G), P.Normal) ∨ (∃ (P : Sylow r G), P.Normal) :=
defect: Only asserts Sylow subgroups exist (always true); normality is missing.; Nonempty (Sylow p G) always holds by Sylow's theorem; normality dropped, conclusion trivial.

N: Prove that if $P \in \operatorname{Syl}_{p}(G)$ and $H$ is a subgroup of $G$ containing $P$ then $P \in \operatorname{Syl}_{p}(H)$.

  (hH : P ≤ H) : IsPGroup p H :=
C:
theorem exercise_4_5_1a {p : ℕ} {G : Type*} [Group G]
  {P : Sylow p G} (H : Subgroup G) (hH : P ≤ H) :
  IsPGroup p (P.subgroupOf H) ∧
  ∀ (Q : Subgroup H), IsPGroup p Q → (P.subgroupOf H) ≤ Q → Q = (P.subgroupOf H) :=
defect: Concludes H is a p-group (false in general) from P being a p-group; not that P is Sylow in H.; Conclusion claims H itself is a p-group, a different (false) statement; Sylow maximality of P also dropped.

N: Let $P$ be a normal Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$ and let $H$ be any subgroup of $G$. Prove that $P \cap H$ is the unique Sylow $p$-subgroup of $H$.

  (P : Sylow p G) [hP : P.Normal] (H : Subgroup G) [Fintype H] :

  Nonempty (Sylow p H) :=
C:
theorem exercise_4_5_33 {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] {p : ℕ}

defect: Nonempty placed inside ∀ R, so existence of a Sylow subgroup equal to P∩H is not asserted; only uniqueness.; Nonempty conjunct inside ∀ R is redundant; existence of a Sylow p-subgroup of H not asserted independently, only uniqueness.

N: Let $R$ be an integral domain. Prove that if the following two conditions hold then $R$ is a Principal Ideal Domain: (i) any two nonzero elements $a$ and $b$ in $R$ have a greatest common divisor which can be written in the form $r a+s b$ for some $r, s \in R$, and (ii) if $a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}, \ldots$ are nonzero elements of $R$ such that $a_{i+1} \mid a_{i}$ for all $i$, then there is a positive integer $N$ such that $a_{n}$ is a unit times $a_{N}$ for all $n \geq N$.
D:
theorem exercise_8_2_4 {R : Type*} [Ring R][NoZeroDivisors R]
  [CancelCommMonoidWithZero R] [GCDMonoid R]
  (h1 : ∀ a b : R, a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → ∃ r s : R, gcd a b = r*a + s*b)
  (h2 : ∀ a : ℕ → R, (∀ i j : ℕ, i < j → a i ∣ a j) →
  ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ u : R, IsUnit u ∧ a n = u * a N) :
  IsPrincipalIdealRing R :=
C:
theorem exercise_8_2_4 {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [GCDMonoid R]
  (h1 : ∀ a b : R, a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → ∃ r s : R, gcd a b = r*a + s*b)
  (h2 : ∀ a : ℕ → R, (∀ i : ℕ, a i ≠ 0 ∧ a (i + 1) ∣ a i) →
  ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ u : R, IsUnit u ∧ a n = u * a N) :
  IsPrincipalIdealRing R :=
defect: Chain condition reversed (a_i divides a_j for i<j) and nonzero terms dropped; also clashing Ring/CancelCommMonoidWithZero structures.; Divisibility chain reversed (a i ∣ a j for i < j, not a (i+1) ∣ a i); nonzero condition dropped; mixed instances.
